claim: Schistosoma mansoni is a parasitic flatworm that causes the major neglected tropical disease schistosomiasis.
source: Schistosoma mansoni is a parasitic flatworm that causes the major neglected tropical disease schistosomiasis.
evidence: This is a well-established fact in the scientific literature about S. mansoni and schistosomiasis.

claim: The miracidium is the first larval stage of the S. mansoni life cycle.
source: The miracidium is the first larval stage of the life cycle.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract and is established knowledge about the schistosome life cycle.

claim: The miracidium swims and infects a freshwater snail.
source: It swims and infects a freshwater snail, transforms into a mother sporocyst
evidence: This is a well-known aspect of the schistosome life cycle.

claim: The miracidium transforms into a mother sporocyst after infecting a snail.
source: It swims and infects a freshwater snail, transforms into a mother sporocyst
evidence: This is established knowledge about schistosome development.

claim: The mother sporocyst's stem cells generate daughter sporocysts that give rise to human-infective cercariae larvae.
source: transforms into a mother sporocyst, where its stem cells generate daughter sporocysts that give rise to human-infective cercariae larvae.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the schistosome life cycle.

claim: The miracidium is composed of approximately 365 cells.
source: There are ~365 nuclei in a miracidium (median = 365, larva #1: 342, larva #2: 365, larva #3: 377).
evidence: This is based on direct counting of nuclei in miracidia specimens as described in the methods.

claim: Single-cell RNA sequencing identified 19 transcriptionally distinct cell clusters in the miracidium.
source: Single-cell RNA sequencing identified 19 transcriptionally distinct cell clusters.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the scRNA-seq analysis presented in the study.

claim: 93% of the cells in the miracidium larva are somatic.
source: In situ hybridisation of tissue-specific genes revealed that 93% of the cells in the larva are somatic
evidence: This is based on in situ hybridization data and cell counting presented in the study.

claim: 57% of cells in the miracidium are neural.
source: 57% neural
evidence: This is based on in situ hybridization and cell counting data.

claim: 19% of cells in the miracidium are muscle.
source: 19% muscle
evidence: This is based on in situ hybridization and cell counting data.

claim: 13% of cells in the miracidium are epidermal or tegument.
source: 13% epidermal or tegument
evidence: This is based on in situ hybridization and cell counting data.

claim: 2% of cells in the miracidium are parenchyma.
source: 2% parenchyma
evidence: This is based on in situ hybridization and cell counting data.

claim: 2% of cells in the miracidium are protonephridia.
source: and 2% protonephridia
evidence: This is based on in situ hybridization and cell counting data.

claim: 7% of cells in the miracidium are stem cells.
source: and 7% are stem.
evidence: This is based on in situ hybridization and cell counting data.

claim: Neurons represent the most diverse somatic cell types in the miracidium.
source: Whereas neurons represent the most diverse somatic cell types
evidence: This is based on the identification of five distinct neuronal clusters in the scRNA-seq data.

claim: There are two main stem cell populations in the miracidium.
source: trajectory analysis of the two main stem cell populations indicates that one of them is the origin of the tegument lineage and the other likely contains pluripotent cells.
evidence: This is based on scRNA-seq clustering and trajectory analysis.

claim: One stem cell population is the origin of the tegument lineage.
source: trajectory analysis of the two main stem cell populations indicates that one of them is the origin of the tegument lineage
evidence: This is based on RNA velocity analysis and expression of tegument-specific transcription factors.

claim: One stem cell population likely contains pluripotent cells.
source: the other likely contains pluripotent cells.
evidence: This is based on expression of germline-specific genes and trajectory analysis.

claim: Each of the two main stem cell populations shows sex-biased transcriptional signatures.
source: Furthermore, unlike the somatic cells, each of these stem populations shows sex-biased transcriptional signatures suggesting a cell-type-specific gene dosage compensation for sex chromosome-linked loci.
evidence: This is based on analysis of sex chromosome gene expression in the scRNA-seq data.

claim: The sex-biased transcriptional signatures in stem cells suggest cell-type-specific gene dosage compensation for sex chromosome-linked loci.
source: suggesting a cell-type-specific gene dosage compensation for sex chromosome-linked loci.
evidence: This is an interpretation based on the observed differences in sex chromosome gene expression between cell types.

claim: Schistosomiasis is responsible for a chronic disease burden equivalent to 1.0–2.6 million Disability Adjusted Life Years annually.
source: which is responsible for a chronic disease burden equivalent to 1.0–2.6 million Disability Adjusted Life Years and over 11,000 human deaths annually (WHO, 2023; IHME, 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations to WHO and IHME reports.

claim: Schistosomiasis causes over 11,000 human deaths annually.
source: and over 11,000 human deaths annually (WHO, 2023; IHME, 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations to WHO and IHME reports.

claim: The life cycle of S. mansoni involves parasitic stages in two hosts: a snail and a mammal.
source: The life cycle of S. mansoni is complex, involving parasitic stages in two hosts (a snail and a mammal)
evidence: This is established knowledge about the schistosome life cycle.

claim: Fertilisation of the S. mansoni zygote occurs inside the female worm.
source: Mature male and female worms reside in the portal veins of the mammalian host, and fertilisation of the zygote occurs inside the female worm (Jurberg et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Jurberg et al., 2009.

claim: S. mansoni embryogenesis proceeds over 6 days as the egg is laid in the host.
source: Embryogenesis proceeds as the egg is laid in the host and continues over the ensuing 6 days (Ashton et al., 2001).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Ashton et al., 2001.

claim: The S. mansoni egg passes through the host vascular endothelium into the intestine and is passed in faeces.
source: During this time, the egg passes through the host vascular endothelium into the intestine and is passed in faeces into the outside environment (Costain et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Costain et al., 2018.

claim: If the miracidium fails to infect a snail within 12 hours it dies.
source: If the miracidium fails to infect a snail within 12 hours it dies.
evidence: This is established knowledge about miracidium biology.

claim: Single-cell RNA-seq studies have identified heterogeneity amongst stem cells that drive schistosome development and reproduction.
source: These studies have opened the door to investigate schistosome developmental cell biology and to identify new targets for controlling infection and transmission of the disease. To date, scRNA-seq studies have identified heterogeneity amongst stem cells that drive schistosome development and reproduction
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous scRNA-seq studies on schistosomes.

claim: Single-cell RNA-seq studies have classified a variety of differentiated cell types across the schistosome life cycle.
source: classified a variety of differentiated cell types across the life cycle
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous scRNA-seq studies on schistosomes.

claim: Single-cell RNA-seq studies have revealed several key genes and their native cell types that are essential for parasite survival and propagation.
source: and revealed several key genes and their native cell types that are essential for parasite survival and propagation (Nanes Sarfati et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Nanes Sarfati et al., 2021.

claim: Single-cell RNA-seq studies for the whole animal have been carried out on the mother sporocyst, schistosomulum, juvenile, and adult stages.
source: Single-cell RNA-seq studies for the whole animal have only been carried out on intra-molluscan and intra-mammalian stages to date: the mother sporocyst (Diaz Soria et al., 2024), the schistosomulum (Diaz Soria et al., 2020), juvenile (3.5 weeks post-infection of mouse, Li et al., 2021), and adult (Wendt et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citations to the respective studies.

claim: There is a lack of single-cell data for the miracidium larva prior to this study.
source: An obvious gap in the coverage of the life cycle is the lack of single-cell data for the earliest developmental time point currently accessible – the miracidium larva
evidence: This is stated as a gap in the literature that this study addresses.

claim: The miracidium is a short-lived, non-feeding stage that relies on internal stores of energy.
source: The miracidium is a short-lived, non-feeding stage that relies on internal stores of energy to sustain swimming, and host location and infection (Maldonado and Acosta-Matienzo, 1948; Chernin, 1968; Pan, 1980).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Maldonado and Acosta-Matienzo, 1948; Chernin, 1968; Pan, 1980.

claim: Eight major systems have been previously identified in the miracidium at the ultrastructural level: musculature, nervous, penetration gland cells, excretory, interstitial (parenchyma), stem/germinal cells, epithelial (ciliary plates and epidermal ridges of the tegument cells), and terebratorium.
source: At the ultrastructural level, a rich set of cell types have been previously identified in the miracidium and classified into eight major systems: musculature, nervous, penetration gland cells, excretory, interstitial (parenchyma), stem/germinal cells, epithelial (ciliary plates and epidermal ridges of the tegument cells), and terebratorium (an apical modified epidermal plate with sensory structures and gland openings) (Pan, 1980).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Pan, 1980.

claim: Single-cell transcriptome data were generated from 20,478 miracidium cells that passed quality control.
source: Using the droplet-based 10X Genomics Chromium platform, transcriptome-sequencing data were generated from a total of 33,391 cells, of which 20,478 passed strict quality control (QC) filters
evidence: This is a direct report of the data generated in the study.

claim: The median number of genes detected per cell was 858.
source: resulting in a median of 858 genes and 1761 median unique molecular identifier (UMI) counts per cell
evidence: This is a direct report of the data quality metrics.

claim: The median UMI count per cell was 1761.
source: resulting in a median of 858 genes and 1761 median unique molecular identifier (UMI) counts per cell
evidence: This is a direct report of the data quality metrics.

claim: The 19 clusters were resolved into two muscle-like clusters (3934 cells).
source: Based on these markers, the 19 clusters were resolved into the following cell populations: two muscle-like (3934 cells)
evidence: This is based on the clustering analysis of the scRNA-seq data.

claim: The 19 clusters included five clusters resembling neurons (3255 cells).
source: five resembling neurons (3255 cells)
evidence: This is based on the clustering analysis of the scRNA-seq data.

claim: The 19 clusters included one ciliary plate cluster (40 cells).
source: one ciliary plate (40 cells)
evidence: This is based on the clustering analysis of the scRNA-seq data.

claim: The 19 clusters included one tegumental cluster (366 cells).
source: one tegumental (366 cells)
evidence: This is based on the clustering analysis of the scRNA-seq data.

claim: The 19 clusters included one protonephridial cluster (539 cells).
source: one protonephridial (539 cells)
evidence: This is based on the clustering analysis of the scRNA-seq data.

claim: The 19 clusters included two parenchymal clusters (1698 cells).
source: two parenchymal (1698 cells)
evidence: This is based on the clustering analysis of the scRNA-seq data.

claim: The 19 clusters included seven clusters resembling stem cells (10,686 cells).
source: and seven clusters resembling stem cells (10,686 cells)
evidence: This is based on the clustering analysis of the scRNA-seq data.

claim: The two muscle clusters were identified based on the expression of paramyosin, troponin t, and titin.
source: The two muscle clusters were identified based on the expression of previously described muscle-specific genes; paramyosin (Smp_085540), troponin t (Smp_179810), and titin (Smp_126240) (Wendt et al., 2020; Diaz Soria et al., 2020; Diaz Soria et al., 2024)
evidence: This is based on expression of known muscle markers in the scRNA-seq data, supported by citations.

claim: In situ hybridisation identified 74 nuclei surrounded by paramyosin transcripts.
source: In situ hybridisation (ISH) (Figure 2B, C; Figure 2—video 1) and image analysis (Figure 2—video 2) identified 74 nuclei surrounded by PRM transcripts (i.e. ~19% of cells in a miracidium are muscle cells).
evidence: This is based on in situ hybridization experiments and cell counting.

claim: Approximately 19% of cells in a miracidium are muscle cells.
source: identified 74 nuclei surrounded by PRM transcripts (i.e. ~19% of cells in a miracidium are muscle cells).
evidence: This is calculated from the count of paramyosin-positive cells relative to total cell number.

claim: The nuclei of the circular muscles formed two distinct bilaterally symmetrical lines that ran peripherally from pole to pole of the larva.
source: The nuclei of the circular muscles formed two distinct bilaterally symmetrical lines that ran peripherally from pole to pole of the larva (~28 nuclei in total).
evidence: This is based on in situ hybridization and imaging data.

claim: There are approximately 28 circular muscle nuclei in the miracidium.
source: The nuclei of the circular muscles formed two distinct bilaterally symmetrical lines that ran peripherally from pole to pole of the larva (~28 nuclei in total).
evidence: This is based on counting of nuclei in in situ hybridization images.

claim: Thirty-three paramyosin-positive nuclei corresponded to longitudinal muscles.
source: Thirty-three more PRM+ nuclei sat regularly spaced between the circular muscle nuclei and corresponded to longitudinal muscles.
evidence: This is based on counting and spatial analysis of in situ hybridization images.

claim: Thirteen paramyosin-positive nuclei formed a unilateral cluster adjacent to the apical gland cell.
source: Another 13 PRM+ nuclei formed a unilateral cluster adjacent to the apical gland cell (identifiable by its four nuclei; Pan, 1980; Figure 2Cii; Figure 2—videos 1 and 2).
evidence: This is based on counting and spatial analysis of in situ hybridization images.

claim: Muscle cluster 1 was distinguished from muscle cluster 2 by markedly higher expression of a Kunitz-type protease inhibitor (Smp_052230).
source: Muscle cluster 1 (2407 cells) was distinguished from muscle cluster 2 by markedly higher expression of a Kunitz-type protease inhibitor (Smp_052230; Figure 2A)
evidence: This is based on differential gene expression analysis in the scRNA-seq data.

claim: Kunitz-type protease inhibitor (Smp_052230) is expressed along the two peripheral lines of circular muscle nuclei.
source: and ISH showed Smp_052230 transcripts along the two peripheral lines of circular muscle nuclei (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is based on in situ hybridization data.

claim: Wnt-11-1 (Smp_156540) was expressed at the posterior pole in seven circular muscle cells.
source: Wnt-11-1 (Smp_156540) was expressed at the posterior pole, in seven of the Kunitz-type protease inhibitor-expressing circular muscle cells (Figure 2D; Figure 2—video 3).
evidence: This is based on in situ hybridization data.

claim: Notum (Smp_015820) was highly expressed in the cluster of 13 muscle nuclei adjacent to the apical gland cell.
source: Notum (Smp_015820) was highly expressed in the cluster of 13 muscle nuclei adjacent to the apical gland cell (Figure 2E).
evidence: This is based on in situ hybridization data.

claim: Muscle cluster 2 was distinguished by higher expression of genes encoding a PDZ domain protein and Calcium-transporting ATPase.
source: Muscle cluster 2 (1355 cells) was distinguished by higher expression of genes encoding a PDZ domain protein (Smp_311170) and Calcium-transporting ATPase (Smp_136710)
evidence: This is based on differential gene expression analysis in the scRNA-seq data.

claim: A putative calcium-activated potassium channel (Smp_156150) and MyoD (Smp_167400) showed expression only in the longitudinal body wall muscles.
source: ISH of the latter two genes showed expression only in the longitudinal BWMs (Figure 2F; Figure 2—video 5).
evidence: This is based on in situ hybridization data.

claim: Five neural clusters were identified expressing the neural markers Complexin, prohormone convertase 2, and Smp_068500.
source: We uncovered five clusters expressing the neural markers Complexin (cpx; Smp_050220), prohormone convertase 2 (PC2; Smp_077980), and Smp_068500 (a neural marker in adult worms, Wendt et al., 2020; Figure 3A).
evidence: This is based on expression of known neural markers in the scRNA-seq data.

claim: Complexin was expressed in and around at least 209 nuclei, indicating that 57% of cells in the miracidium were neurons.
source: Complexin was expressed in and around at least 209 nuclei, indicating that 57% of cells in the miracidium were neurons
evidence: This is based on in situ hybridization and cell counting.

claim: 129 complexin-positive nuclei formed the nuclear rind of the brain.
source: out of which 129 cpx+ nuclei formed the nuclear rind of the brain (or neural mass/ring)
evidence: This is based on in situ hybridization and cell counting.

claim: 80 complexin-positive nuclei were situated peripherally, either anterior or posterior to the brain.
source: and the remaining 80 were situated peripherally, either anterior or posterior to the brain (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is based on in situ hybridization and cell counting.

claim: Neuron cluster 1 was large (1470 cells) and expressed neuron-marker complexin, the neuroendocrine precursor 7B2, and an uncharacterised gene (Smp_068500).
source: Neuron cluster 1 was large (1470 cells), and expressed neuron-marker complexin, the neuroendocrine precursor 7B2 (Smp_073270) and an uncharacterised gene (Smp_068500).
evidence: This is based on the clustering and marker gene analysis of the scRNA-seq data.

claim: Subclustering of Neuron 1 revealed subpopulations expressing neuropeptide precursor genes PWamide, Neuropeptide F, and Neuropeptide Y.
source: Three subclusters of Neuron 1 expressed neuropeptide precursor genes amongst their top 5 markers; PWamide (Smp_340860) (Wang et al., 2016) in subcluster 14, Neuropeptide F (Smp_088360) in subcluster 8, and Neuropeptide Y (Smp_159950) in subcluster 13 (Figure 3—figure supplement 1)
evidence: This is based on subclustering analysis of Neuron 1 using the SAM algorithm.

claim: A subcluster of Neuron 1 is composed of putative photoreceptor cells expressing two opsins.
source: Another subcluster was composed of putative photoreceptor cells (subcluster 7, Figure 3—figure supplement 1, Supplementary file 1f) because their top 10 markers include two opsins (Smp_180350 and Smp_332250) – identified here as a rhabdomeric opsin and a peropsin, respectively (Figure 3—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is based on subclustering analysis and expression of opsin genes.

claim: Neuron 2 expressed two rhabdomeric opsins (Smp_180030 and Smp_104210).
source: Neuron 2 expressed two further rhabdomeric opsins (Smp_180030 and Smp_104210; Figure 3—figure supplement 3)
evidence: This is based on gene expression analysis and phylogenetic classification of opsins.

claim: The most expressed marker in Neuron 2 was Smp_201600, identified as the neuropeptide precursor NPP-43.
source: but across the cluster of 282 cells, the most expressed marker was Smp_201600, identified as the neuropeptide precursor NPP-43 (Koziol et al., 2016).
evidence: This is based on marker gene analysis and citation to Koziol et al., 2016.

claim: ISH revealed three strongly Smp_201600-positive cells with nuclei in a median posterior location of the brain.
source: ISH revealed three strongly Smp_201600+ cells, with nuclei in a median posterior location of the brain, and three cells with weaker expression in a more anterior position (Figure 3C, Figure 3—video 1).
evidence: This is based on in situ hybridization data.

claim: Neuron 3 was a small cluster (47 cells) expressing complexin and 7B2.
source: Neuron 3 was a small cluster (47 cells) expressing complexin and 7B2.
evidence: This is based on clustering and marker gene analysis of the scRNA-seq data.

claim: The neuropeptide precursor NPP-26 (Smp_071050) was unique to and highly expressed throughout the Neuron 3 population.
source: The neuropeptide precursor NPP-26 (Smp_071050) (Koziol et al., 2016) was unique to and highly expressed throughout this population (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is based on marker gene analysis and citation to Koziol et al., 2016.

claim: ISH showed NPP-26 expression in approximately 6 cells with projections that extended into the brain and to the periphery.
source: ISH showed expression in ~6 cells with projections that extended into the brain and to the periphery, three of which sat adjacent to three Neuron 2 cells.
evidence: This is based on in situ hybridization data.

claim: Neuron 4 formed a large (1140 cells), discrete cluster.
source: Neuron 4 formed a large (1140 cells), discrete cluster.
evidence: This is based on clustering analysis of the scRNA-seq data.

claim: The top marker for Neuron 4 was an uncharacterised gene, Smp_319480, similar to human mTORC1 based on protein-structure prediction.
source: The top marker was an uncharacterised gene, Smp_319480 (Figure 3A), that, based on protein-structure prediction using I-TASSER (Yang and Zhang, 2015), was similar to human mTORC1 (protein database [PDB] entry 5H64; TM-score 0.85).
evidence: This is based on marker gene analysis and computational protein structure prediction.

claim: In situ expression of Smp_319480 revealed approximately 26 cells: four at the anterior end and approximately 22 lateral and directly posterior to the brain.
source: In situ expression revealed ~26 Smp_319480+ cells; four at the anterior end, with projections leading to the body wall in the first tier of ciliary plates, and ~22 sat lateral and directly posterior to the brain.
evidence: This is based on in situ hybridization data.

claim: Twenty-three multi-ciliated nerve endings formed a girdle around the larva between the second and third tiers of ciliary plates.
source: Twenty-three multi-ciliated nerve endings formed a girdle around the larva between the second and third tiers of ciliary plates (Figure 3—figure supplement 2C)
evidence: This is based on antibody staining data.

claim: Smp_319480 transcripts were expressed at the base of the multi-ciliated nerve endings.
source: and Smp_319480 transcripts were expressed at the base of these cilia (Figure 3—figure supplement 2D)
evidence: This is based on in situ hybridization data.

claim: Polycystin 1 (Smp_165230) and Polycystin 2 (Smp_165660) are co-expressed in many Neuron 4 cells.
source: Two genes, identified as top markers and co-expressed in many Neuron 4 cells, encode likely orthologues of Polycystin 1 (Smp_165230) and Polycystin 2 (Smp_165660) (Figure 3—figure supplement 5)
evidence: This is based on marker gene analysis and homology inference.

claim: Neuron 5 cluster comprised 276 cells.
source: Neuron 5 cluster comprised 276 cells.
evidence: This is based on clustering analysis of the scRNA-seq data.

claim: An EF-hand domain-containing protein, Smp_343710, was highly expressed in 55% of Neuron 5 cells.
source: An EF-hand domain-containing protein, Smp_343710, was highly expressed in 55% of these cells.
evidence: This is based on marker gene analysis of the scRNA-seq data.

claim: ISH showed Smp_343710 expression in 10–20 cells whose nuclei sat outside of, and anterior to, the brain, in and around the paired lateral glands.
source: ISH showed expression in 10–20 cells whose nuclei sat outside of, and anterior to, the brain, in and around the paired lateral glands and their secretory ducts (Figure 3—video 6).
evidence: This is based on in situ hybridization data.

claim: Smp_343710 was also expressed in a pair of bilaterally symmetrical bulbous protrusions (lateral sensory papilla).
source: There was also expression in a pair of bilaterally symmetrical bulbous protrusions (called lateral sensory papilla and thought to be depth sensors, Pan, 1980; Figure 3F).
evidence: This is based on in situ hybridization data and citation to Pan, 1980.

claim: Plate-based single-cell RNA-seq was carried out on 37 manually selected gland cells.
source: To characterise the transcriptomes of the gland cells, we carried out plate-based single-cell RNA-seq (New England BioLabs) on 37 manually selected gland cells (Supplementary file 1h).
evidence: This is a description of the experimental methods used.

claim: The gland cells showed co-expression of neural markers (Complexin and 7B2) and muscle markers (Myosin light chain 1, Troponin t, and Actin-2).
source: The gland cells showed co-expression of neural markers (Complexin and 7B2) and muscle markers Myosin light chain 1 (Smp_045200), Troponin t (Smp_179810), and Actin-2 (Smp_307020) (Figure 3—figure supplement 6).
evidence: This is based on plate-based scRNA-seq data.

claim: Five venom antigen-like (VAL) genes were expressed in the gland cells.
source: Five venom antigen-like (VAL) genes (belonging to the SCP/TAPS or (CAP) superfamily) were expressed in the gland cells: Smp_120670 (VAL 5) and Smp_070250 (VAL 15) in over 60% of the gland cells, and Smp_176180 (VAL 9), Smp_002630 (VAL 2), and Smp_331830 (SCP protein) in less than 50%.
evidence: This is based on plate-based scRNA-seq data.

claim: A small cluster of 40 cells was identified as ciliary plates based on expression of a 16-kDa calcium-binding protein (CaBP) and p25 alpha.
source: A small cluster of 40 cells (almost exclusively from the unsorted samples) was identified near the tegument cluster (Figure 1C). The top markers were Smp_096390, a 16-kDa calcium-binding protein (CaBP) and p25 alpha (Smp_097490, a marker for ciliated neurons in adult worms, Wendt et al., 2020; Figure 3A).
evidence: This is based on clustering and marker gene analysis, with citation to Wendt et al., 2020.

claim: In situ hybridisation revealed CaBP and p25 alpha expression in the ciliary plates.
source: In situ hybridisation revealed CaBP and p25 alpha expression in the ciliary plates; epithelial cells with thousands of motile cilia used for swimming (Figure 3G and Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is based on in situ hybridization data.

claim: CaBP and p25 alpha were also expressed in six previously undescribed submuscular cells that sent a projection out to the exterior.
source: Both genes were also expressed in six previously undescribed cells that sent a projection out to the exterior (between the first and second tiers of ciliary plates as seen with phalloidin staining, Figure 3G) and whose nuclei sat below the body wall musculature (Figure 3—videos 2; 3 ; Figure 3—figure supplement 2F).
evidence: This is based on in situ hybridization and imaging data.

claim: A cluster of 366 cells was identified as tegumental based on the expression of markers for tegument in the adult worm.
source: We identified a cluster of 366 cells as tegumental based on the expression of markers for tegument (skin) in the adult worm (Wendt et al., 2020), for example genes encoding dynein light chain (Smp_302860, Smp_200180), a DUF3421 domain-containing protein (Smp_331910), and micro exon gene MEG6 (Smp_163710).
evidence: This is based on marker gene analysis and citation to Wendt et al., 2020.

claim: Meg6 (Smp_163710) was expressed in 66% of the cells in the tegument cluster.
source: Meg6 (Smp_163710) was expressed in 66% of the cells in this cluster
evidence: This is based on marker gene analysis of the scRNA-seq data.

claim: ISH showed 46 Meg6-positive cells with nuclei in the posterior two-thirds of the larva.
source: ISH showed 46 Meg6+ cells, and the nuclei were in the posterior two-thirds of the larva.
evidence: This is based on in situ hybridization and cell counting.

claim: The Meg6-positive cells sat below the body wall muscle, and cytoplasmic protrusions reached between muscle filaments and formed the epidermal ridges between the ciliary plates.
source: The nuclei sat below the BWM, and cytoplasmic protrusions reached between muscle filaments and formed the epidermal ridges between the ciliary plates (Figure 4C, D).
evidence: This is based on in situ hybridization and imaging data.

claim: There were 536 cells in the protonephridial cluster.
source: There were 536 cells in the protonephridial cluster
evidence: This is based on clustering analysis of the scRNA-seq data.

claim: The protonephridial cluster expressed genes common to excretory systems in other animals, such as nephrin and odd-skipped-related.
source: expressing genes common to excretory systems in other animals (Gąsiorowski et al., 2021), for example, the structural protein nephrin (Smp_130070) and the transcription factor odd-skipped-related (Smp_152210).
evidence: This is based on marker gene analysis and citation to Gąsiorowski et al., 2021.

claim: Eighty percent of the protonephridial cells expressed the protonephridia marker Smp_335600 (ShKT-domain-containing protein).
source: Eighty percent of the cells expressed the protonephridia marker Smp_335600 (ShKT-domain-containing protein) (Nanes Sarfati et al., 2021; Figure 4A).
evidence: This is based on marker gene analysis and citation to Nanes Sarfati et al., 2021.

claim: Smp_335600 was expressed around six nuclei in a bilaterally symmetrical pattern.
source: Smp_335600 was expressed around six nuclei in a bilaterally symmetrical pattern (Figure 4Ei; Figure 4—video 1).
evidence: This is based on in situ hybridization data.

claim: Smp_335600 transcripts were distributed along the s-shaped path of an excretory tubule, connecting the anterior and posterior flame cells.
source: On each side, Smp_335600 transcripts were distributed along the s-shaped path of an excretory tubule, passing its nucleus, and connecting the anterior and posterior flame cells (Figure 4Ei).
evidence: This is based on in situ hybridization data.

claim: Two parenchyma clusters were identified (1093 cells from Parenchyma 1 and 605 cells from Parenchyma 2).
source: We identified two clusters of cells (1093 cells from Parenchyma 1 and 605 cells from Parenchyma 2) that were transcriptionally similar to the parenchymal cells found in later developmental stages
evidence: This is based on clustering analysis of the scRNA-seq data.

claim: The parenchyma clusters expressed hypothetical protein (Smp_063330), cathepsin B-like cysteine proteinase (Smp_141610), and serpin (Smp_090080).
source: for example, they express hypothetical protein (Smp_063330), cathepsin B-like cysteine proteinase (Smp_141610), and serpin (Smp_090080) (Diaz Soria et al., 2020; Wendt et al., 2020; Diaz Soria et al., 2024).
evidence: This is based on marker gene analysis and citations to previous studies.

claim: A gene encoding a Zinc transporter Slc39a7 (Smp_318890) was a top marker for both parenchyma clusters.
source: A gene encoding a Zinc transporter Slc39a7 (Smp_318890) was a top marker for both clusters
evidence: This is based on marker gene analysis of the scRNA-seq data.

claim: Smp_318890 was expressed in seven to nine cells: two located anteriorly on either side of the brain and five to seven located posterior to the brain.
source: with expression confirmed in situ within seven to nine cells; two of which were located anteriorly on either side of the brain and five to seven located posterior to the brain (Figure 4B, F).
evidence: This is based on in situ hybridization data.

claim: Parenchyma cells have long cytoplasmic protrusions that reach between all the other cells, filling the intercellular space.
source: These parenchyma cells have long cytoplasmic protrusions that reach between all the other cells, filling the intercellular space (Figure 4Fii, iii; Figure 4—videos 2; 3).
evidence: This is based on in situ hybridization and imaging data.

claim: Stem cells were identified based on the expression of known stem cell markers for the mother sporocyst stage, such as ago2-1, nanos-2, fgfrA, fgfrB, klf, and hesl.
source: We identified stem cells based on the expression of known stem cell markers for the mother sporocyst stage, for example ago2-1 (Smp_179320), nanos-2 (Smp_051920), fgfrA (Smp_175590), fgfrB (Smp_157300), klf (Smp_172480), and hesl (Smp_024860) (Wang et al., 2013; Wang et al., 2018; Figure 5A).
evidence: This is based on marker gene analysis and citations to Wang et al., 2013; Wang et al., 2018.

claim: Seven stem cell clusters were identified by expression of ago2-1 (10,686 cells).
source: In the miracidium, we identified seven stem cell clusters by expression of ago2-1 (10,686 cells)
evidence: This is based on clustering analysis of the scRNA-seq data.

claim: Stems A and B are klf+ and nanos-2+ (Kappa-like).
source: Stems A and B are klf+ and nanos-2+ (i.e. Kappa-like)
evidence: This is based on marker gene expression analysis.

claim: Stems C and D are nanos-2+, fgfrA+, fgfrB+, and hesl+ (resembling both Delta and Phi).
source: Stems C and D are nanos-2+, fgfrA+, fgfrB+, and hesl+ (i.e. they resembled both Delta and Phi) (Figure 5A, Figure 5—figure supplement 1)
evidence: This is based on marker gene expression analysis.

claim: The Delta/Phi- and Kappa-like populations are each composed of two well-separated clusters that can be distinguished based on the expression of sex-linked genes.
source: Working with the latest version of S. mansoni genome (v10), where the sex chromosomes Z and W have been resolved (Buddenborg et al., 2021), we were able to determine that the Delta/Phi- and Kappa-like populations are each composed of two well-separated clusters that can be distinguished based on the expression of sex-linked genes (Figure 5A; Figure 5—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is based on analysis of sex chromosome gene expression using genome version 10, with citation to Buddenborg et al., 2021.

claim: When all Z-specific region (ZSR) and W-specific region (WSR) genes were removed from the dataset and the cells reclustered, the two Delta/Phi-like and two Kappa-like clusters each collapsed into single stem cell clusters.
source: When all Z-specific region (ZSR) and W-specific region (WSR) genes were removed from the dataset and the cells reclustered, the two Delta/Phi-like and two Kappa-like clusters each collapsed into single stem cell clusters, giving five stem cell clusters in total (i.e. Delta/Phi, Kappa, E, F, and G; Figure 5B, Figure 5—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is based on re-clustering analysis after removing sex chromosome genes.

claim: Sex-linked gene dosage is not fully compensated in the miracidium.
source: These findings suggest that sex-linked gene dosage is not fully compensated in the miracidium, and there may be tissue-specific variation.
evidence: This is an interpretation based on the observed differences in ZSR gene expression between male and female cells.

claim: Ago2-1+ cells were distributed lateral and posterior to the brain.
source: Ago2-1+ cells were distributed lateral and posterior to the brain (Figure 5Ci)
evidence: This is based on in situ hybridization data.

claim: The number of Ago2-1+ cells ranged from 20 to 29, with a median of 23.
source: and there was variation in the number between larvae, ranging from 20 to 29 (segmentation of Ago2-1+ nuclei in 5 larvae, median = 23, mean = 23.4) (i.e. ~7% of cells that make up the larva are stem cells).
evidence: This is based on counting of Ago2-1+ cells in in situ hybridization images.

claim: Approximately 7% of cells that make up the larva are stem cells.
source: (i.e. ~7% of cells that make up the larva are stem cells).
evidence: This is calculated from the count of Ago2-1+ cells relative to total cell number.

claim: Cells in the Delta/Phi-like cluster expressed a canonical p53 tumour suppressor family gene (p53-1, Smp_139530) as a top marker.
source: Cells in the Delta/Phi-like cluster expressed a canonical p53 tumour suppressor family gene (p53-1, Smp_139530) as a top marker
evidence: This is based on marker gene analysis of the scRNA-seq data.

claim: In situ expression showed 12–14 p53-1+ cells.
source: in situ expression showed 12–14 p53-1+ cells (segmentation of three larvae) (Figure 5D).
evidence: This is based on in situ hybridization and cell counting.

claim: Cells in the Kappa-like cluster expressed Uridine phosphorylase A (UPPA, Smp_308145) as a top marker.
source: Cells in the Kappa-like cluster expressed Uridine phosphorylase A (UPPA, Smp_308145) as a top marker
evidence: This is based on marker gene analysis of the scRNA-seq data.

claim: In situ expression showed eight to nine UPPA+ cells located amongst the p53-1+ cells.
source: in situ expression showed eight to nine UPPA+ cells, and they were located amongst the p53-1+ cells (segmentation of three larvae) (Figure 5D).
evidence: This is based on in situ hybridization and cell counting.

claim: DNA replication does not take place in the stem or somatic cells during the free-swimming miracidium stage.
source: A lack of EdU incorporation into miracidia cells (Figure 5—figure supplement 5) indicated that DNA replication does not take place in the stem or somatic cells during this free-swimming stage.
evidence: This is based on EdU incorporation experiments.

claim: The first stem cells start proliferating in the mother sporocyst approximately 20 hr post-infection.
source: As the first stem cells start proliferating in the mother sporocyst ~20 hr post-infection (Wang et al., 2013)
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Wang et al., 2013.

claim: Both stem cell populations pause cell division for at least 26 hr.
source: this suggests that both stem cell populations pause cell division for at least 26 hr.
evidence: This is an inference based on the lack of EdU incorporation in miracidia and the timing of proliferation in mother sporocysts.

claim: Many top markers for the Delta/Phi and Kappa stem clusters were ribosomal proteins.
source: Many top markers for the Delta/Phi and Kappa stem clusters were ribosomal proteins (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is based on marker gene analysis of the scRNA-seq data.

claim: STRING analysis showed that most of the top 100 markers of each stem cluster formed large single networks enriched for genes involved in translation, ribosome biogenesis, and gene expression.
source: STRING analysis showed that most of the top 100 markers of each cluster both formed large single networks enriched for genes involved in translation, ribosome biogenesis, and gene expression, and this was particularly striking in the Delta/Phi cluster (Figure 5—figure supplement 6).
evidence: This is based on STRING protein-protein interaction analysis.

claim: Six transcription factors were upregulated in Delta/Phi: lin-39, tiptop, hes-related, p53-1, Zfp-1, and a putative homothorax homeobox protein/six-3–1.
source: Amongst the top genes differentially expressed between Kappa and Delta/Phi (Figure 5—figure supplement 7A; Supplementary file 1n) were six transcription factors upregulated in Delta/Phi: an orthologue of lin-39 (Smp_247590), tiptop (Smp_180690), hes-related (Smp_024860), p53-1 (Smp_139530), Zfp-1 (Smp_145470), and a putative homothorax homeobox protein/six-3–1 (Smp_147790).
evidence: This is based on differential gene expression analysis between stem clusters.

claim: The simultaneous co-expression of multiple transcription factors indicates a multipotent progenitor stage.
source: The simultaneous co-expression of multiple transcription factors indicates a multipotent progenitor stage (Kumar et al., 2017).
evidence: This is an interpretation based on known biology of multipotent cells, supported by citation to Kumar et al., 2017.

claim: Genes involved in glycolysis and lipid metabolism were enriched in, or specific to, Kappa cells.
source: Enriched in, or specific to, Kappa cells were genes involved in glycolysis and lipid metabolism, that is malate dehydrogenase (Smp_129610), 14 kDa fatty acid-binding protein (Smp_095360) and a very long-chain fatty acid elongase (Smp_051810).
evidence: This is based on differential gene expression analysis between stem clusters.

claim: GO analysis showed that the most significantly upregulated genes in Delta/Phi were related to the structural component of the ribosome and translation.
source: GO analysis of differentially expressed genes (Supplementary file 1o) revealed that the most significantly upregulated genes in Delta/Phi were related to the structural component of the ribosome and translation; these are the first markers of a pre-activation stage in stem cells (Shin et al., 2015).
evidence: This is based on GO analysis of differentially expressed genes, with citation to Shin et al., 2015.

claim: GO analysis showed that upregulated genes in Kappa are involved in transcription and metabolism, indicating quiescent rather than primed and activated stem cells.
source: Whereas GO analysis showed that upregulated genes in Kappa are involved in transcription and metabolism (Figure 5—figure supplement 7B), which indicated quiescent rather than primed and activated stem cells (Llorens-Bobadilla et al., 2015).
evidence: This is based on GO analysis of differentially expressed genes, with citation to Llorens-Bobadilla et al., 2015.

claim: The Delta/Phi stem population simultaneously co-expressed three transcription factors known to be specific to the flatworm tegument/epidermal lineage: p53-1, zfp-1, and six3-1.
source: The Delta/Phi stem population simultaneously co-expressed three transcription factors that are known to be specific to the flatworm tegument/epidermal lineage, that is p53-1, zfp-1, and six3-1 (Cheng et al., 2018; Collins et al., 2016; Wendt et al., 2018).
evidence: This is based on marker gene expression analysis, with citations to Cheng et al., 2018; Collins et al., 2016; Wendt et al., 2018.

claim: The Delta/Phi stem population may have been the origin of the miracidia tegument cells and may be the source of new tegument cells in the mother sporocyst stage.
source: This suggests that the Delta/Phi stem population may have been the origin of the miracidia tegument cells and may be the source of new tegument cells in the mother sporocyst stage.
evidence: This is an inference based on expression of tegument-specific transcription factors.

claim: RNA velocity analysis indicates the progression of some miracidia Delta/Phi stem cells towards the miracidia tegument cells.
source: The velocity field and latent time representations indicate the progression of some miracidia Delta/Phi stem cells towards the miracidia tegument cells and a high speed of differentiation was inferred from the miracidia tegument cells to the sporocyst tegument (Figure 6B, C).
evidence: This is based on RNA velocity analysis of combined miracidia and sporocyst data.

claim: A high speed of differentiation was inferred from the miracidia tegument cells to the sporocyst tegument.
source: and a high speed of differentiation was inferred from the miracidia tegument cells to the sporocyst tegument (Figure 6B, C).
evidence: This is based on RNA velocity analysis of combined miracidia and sporocyst data.

claim: The miracidia tegument cluster may contain cells that range from post-mitotic stem cell progeny to tegument progenitors to terminally differentiated tegumental cells.
source: This suggests that the miracidia tegument cluster may contain cells that range from post-mitotic stem cell progeny to tegument progenitors to terminally differentiated tegumental cells.
evidence: This is an inference based on RNA velocity analysis.

claim: P53-1 was induced in the Delta/Phi stem cells but repressed in some miracidia tegument cells.
source: P53-1 (Smp_139530) was induced in the Delta/Phi stem cells but repressed in some miracidia tegument cells and expression decreased in a continuum across the miracidia tegument cells (Figure 6D).
evidence: This is based on RNA velocity analysis.

claim: Zfp-1 showed a similar expression pattern to p53-1, except that the predominance of spliced copies suggested that transcription happened earlier, during embryogenesis.
source: The flatworm-specific transcription factor Zfp-1 (Smp_145470) showed a similar expression pattern to p53-1, except that the predominance of spliced copies (Figure 6E) suggested that transcription happened earlier, during embryogenesis.
evidence: This is based on RNA velocity analysis and interpretation of spliced vs unspliced transcript ratios.

claim: In the Kappa stem population, there was transcription and expression of genes detected in germline stem cells and germ cells in the intra-mammalian stages of the life cycle.
source: In the Kappa stem population, there was transcription and expression of genes detected in germline stem cells and germ cells in the intra-mammalian stages of the life cycle (Wang et al., 2018; Li et al., 2021).
evidence: This is based on marker gene expression analysis, with citations to Wang et al., 2018; Li et al., 2021.

claim: A second P53 homologue, p53-2 (Smp_136160), was highly expressed and actively transcribed in Kappa cells.
source: A second P53 homologue, p53-2 (Smp_136160), was highly expressed and actively transcribed in Kappa cells (Figure 6F).
evidence: This is based on RNA velocity analysis.

claim: In adults, p53-2 is enriched in reproductive organs and has a genotoxic stress response that is thought to defend the integrity of the genome by eliminating germ cells that have acquired mutations.
source: In adults, this gene is enriched in reproductive organs and has a genotoxic stress response that is thought to defend the integrity of the genome by eliminating germ cells that have acquired mutations (Wendt et al., 2022).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Wendt et al., 2022.

claim: Germline-specific regulatory genes eled, onecut1, irx, akkn, and boule are expressed solely in Kappa cells.
source: Also expressed solely in Kappa cells (though some at low levels) are the germline-specific regulatory genes eled (Smp_041540) (Figure 6G), onecut1 (Smp_196950), irx (Smp_063520), akkn (Smp_131630), and boule (Smp_144860) (expressed in the female Kappa cells and Stem E, Figure 6—figure supplement 5; Wang et al., 2018; Li et al., 2021)
evidence: This is based on marker gene expression analysis, with citations to Wang et al., 2018; Li et al., 2021.

claim: The Delta/Phi population is the origin of the tegumental lineage and likely contributes to extra-embryonic somatic tissues during intra-molluscan development.
source: Together, these data suggest that the Delta/Phi population is the origin of the tegumental lineage and likely contributes to extra-embryonic somatic tissues during intra-molluscan development
evidence: This is an inference based on RNA velocity analysis and marker gene expression.

claim: The Kappa population likely contains pluripotent cells that will contribute to the development of cercariae and the germline in intra-mammalian stages.
source: while the Kappa population likely contains pluripotent cells that will contribute to the development of cercariae and the germline in intra-mammalian stages (Figure 7).
evidence: This is an inference based on expression of germline-specific genes and trajectory analysis.

claim: The miracidium, with its diversity of differentiated cells present in relatively low numbers, makes a simple and tractable system with which to gain a fundamental understanding of the biology and spatial architecture of schistosome cells.
source: The miracidium, therefore, with its diversity of differentiated cells present in relatively low numbers, makes a simple and tractable system with which to gain a fundamental understanding of the biology and spatial architecture of schistosome cells, and their transcriptomes.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the findings of the study.

claim: Compared to later life cycle stages, the miracidium is a simple stage of the life cycle.
source: Compared to later life cycle stages, where the cercariae is made up of ~1600 cells, the schistosomulum ~900 (Diaz Soria et al., 2020) and the adults tens of thousands of cells (unpublished data), the miracidium is a simple stage of the life cycle.
evidence: This is based on comparison of cell numbers across life stages, with citation to Diaz Soria et al., 2020.

claim: The cercariae is made up of approximately 1600 cells.
source: where the cercariae is made up of ~1600 cells
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge.

claim: The schistosomulum is made up of approximately 900 cells.
source: the schistosomulum ~900 (Diaz Soria et al., 2020)
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Diaz Soria et al., 2020.

claim: Adult schistosomes are made up of tens of thousands of cells.
source: and the adults tens of thousands of cells (unpublished data)
evidence: This is stated as unpublished data.

claim: The stem cells accounted for approximately 52% of the scRNA-seq data.
source: Some cell types were preferentially recovered, for example the stem cells; ISH revealed that they comprise only 7% of the total cell number in the larva, yet they accounted for ~52% of the scRNA-seq data (Supplementary file 1q).
evidence: This is based on comparison of in situ counts and scRNA-seq data.

claim: Preferential recovery of certain cell types may be due to differences in the robustness of different cell types to dissociation, cell sorting, and/or the microfluidics of the 10X GEM capture process.
source: Preferential recovery may be due to differences in the robustness of different cell types to dissociation, cell sorting, and/or the microfluidics of the 10X GEM capture process.
evidence: This is speculation about the causes of preferential recovery.

claim: The ciliary plates were only found in sufficient numbers to be defined as a cluster in unsorted samples.
source: The ciliary plates, for instance, were only found in sufficient numbers to be defined as a cluster in unsorted samples.
evidence: This is based on comparison of sorted and unsorted samples in the scRNA-seq data.

claim: There are clear benefits to including unsorted cell samples to discover the diversity of cell types in a tissue, organ, or organism, especially when cell types may be fragile, sticky, or unusually shaped.
source: Therefore, there are clear benefits to including unsorted cell samples to discover the diversity of cell types in a tissue, organ, or organism, especially when cell types may be fragile, sticky, or unusually shaped.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the observation that some cell types were only recovered in unsorted samples.

claim: The penetration glands were not captured in the 10X data, possibly because of their large size and irregular shape.
source: These cells were easily identified after dissociation by their distinct flask shape but were not identifiable in these 10X data. Perhaps, because of their large size (20 × 50 µm) and irregular shape, they were not incorporated into the 10X GEMs.
evidence: This is speculation about why gland cells were not captured in the 10X data.

claim: Plate-based scRNA-seq was used for the penetration glands to complete the cell-type transcriptome atlas for all known cell types.
source: Therefore, we used plate-based scRNA-seq for the penetration glands to complete the cell-type transcriptome atlas for all known cell types.
evidence: This is a description of the experimental approach used.

claim: The two muscle clusters correspond to the circular and longitudinal muscles that comprise the orthogonal body wall muscles of the miracidium.
source: The two muscle clusters in our dataset correspond to the circular and longitudinal muscles that comprise the orthogonal BWMs of the miracidium.
evidence: This is based on in situ hybridization and marker gene expression analysis.

claim: Differences between circular and longitudinal muscle transcriptomes have also been observed in planaria.
source: We identified differences between circular and longitudinal muscle transcriptomes that have also been observed in planaria; for example MyoD and Wnt-11-1 are expressed in longitudinal and circular muscles, respectively (Scimone et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Scimone et al., 2017.

claim: Posterior Wnt signalling and anterior Wnt inhibition are commonly observed features of anterior–posterior body patterning in animals.
source: Posterior Wnt signalling and anterior Wnt inhibition are commonly observed features of anterior–posterior body patterning in animals (Petersen and Reddien, 2009).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Petersen and Reddien, 2009.

claim: The expression of Wnt-11-1 and Notum in the circular muscles at opposite poles of the miracidium suggests these muscles are involved in defining the anterior–posterior axis.
source: The expression of Wnt-11-1 and a Wnt inhibitor, Notum, in the circular muscles at opposite poles of the miracidium suggested these muscles are involved in defining the anterior–posterior axis.
evidence: This is an inference based on the expression patterns of Wnt signaling genes.

claim: The unilateral, asymmetrical expression of Notum at the anterior end is suggestive of a dorso–ventral axis and/or a left–right axis.
source: Furthermore, the unilateral, asymmetrical expression of Notum at the anterior end is suggestive of a dorso–ventral axis and/or a left–right axis, neither of which have been identified in the miracidium before.
evidence: This is an inference based on the asymmetric expression pattern of Notum.

claim: Many axial patterning genes expressed in planaria muscles are essential for patterning during regeneration.
source: Many axial patterning genes expressed in planaria muscles are essential for patterning during regeneration (Witchley et al., 2013; Vogg et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Witchley et al., 2013; Vogg et al., 2014.

claim: The expression of axial patterning gene orthologues in S. mansoni muscles suggests that these genes may regulate stem cells during homeostasis in the adult.
source: The expression of orthologues in S. mansoni muscles, a nonregenerative animal, suggests that these genes may regulate stem cells during homeostasis in the adult (Wendt et al., 2020).
evidence: This is an inference based on expression patterns, with citation to Wendt et al., 2020.

claim: The expression of axial patterning genes in the muscles of the larva suggests they will provide positional information to the stem cells of the mother sporocyst in the axial patterning of the daughter sporocysts.
source: As the body axes of the miracidium were defined during embryogenesis, the expression of these genes in the muscles of the larva suggests they will provide positional information to the stem cells of the mother sporocyst in the axial patterning of the daughter sporocysts.
evidence: This is an inference based on the expression of axial patterning genes.

claim: The nervous system accounts for over 50% of cells that make up the larva and is the most transcriptionally heterogeneous tissue.
source: The nervous system accounts for over 50% of cells that make up the larva and is the most transcriptionally heterogeneous tissue, as observed in other animals (Siebert et al., 2019; Vergara et al., 2021).
evidence: This is based on cell counting and clustering analysis, with citations to Siebert et al., 2019; Vergara et al., 2021.

claim: At the end of embryogenesis, at hatching, most of the miracidia neurons are fully differentiated and form the functional neural circuits of the larva.
source: At the end of embryogenesis, at hatching, most of the miracidia neurons are fully differentiated and form the functional neural circuits of the larva.
evidence: This is an inference based on the presence of discrete, well-defined neural cell clusters in the scRNA-seq data.

claim: The location and shape of Neuron 4 cells resemble that of the bipolar ganglion cells with multi-ciliated nerve endings described by Pan, 1980.
source: In situ validation of marker genes revealed many of the nerves identified ultrastructurally; for example, the location and shape of Neuron 4 cells resemble that of the bipolar ganglion cells with multi-ciliated nerve endings described by Pan, 1980.
evidence: This is based on comparison of in situ data with previous ultrastructural descriptions, with citation to Pan, 1980.

claim: The gene expression profile of Neuron 4 cells in the miracidium suggests they could function as flow and/or vibration sensors.
source: The gene expression profile of Neuron 4 cells in the miracidium suggests they could function as flow and/or vibration sensors and may be specified by a Sox transcription factor.
evidence: This is an inference based on the expression of polycystin genes and comparison with known functions in other organisms.

claim: The multi-ciliated receptors of Neuron 4 degenerate 12 hr after the miracidia transform into a mother sporocyst.
source: These multi-ciliated receptors degenerate 12 hr after the miracidia transform into a mother sporocyst (Poteaux et al., 2023).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Poteaux et al., 2023.

claim: The six submuscular cells that express ciliary plate markers could play a role in the development and functioning of the ciliary plates.
source: The expression of these genes in both the ciliary plates and the submuscular cells suggests that these latter cells are transcriptionally similar and might play a role in the development and functioning of the ciliary plates.
evidence: This is an inference based on shared marker gene expression.

claim: The submuscular cells' projection into the external environment suggests a sensory role.
source: Their projection into the external environment suggests a sensory role
evidence: This is an inference based on the anatomical observation.

claim: The submuscular cells could function similarly to the ciliomotor pacemaker neurons in Platynereis larvae.
source: which, together with their location between the first and second tier of ciliary plates, could suggest a role in coordinating the movement of the motile cilia across the plates and tiers in response to sensory cues (i.e. similar in function to the ciliomotor pacemaker neurons in Platynereis larvae, Verasztó et al., 2017).
evidence: This is speculation based on comparison with a similar cell type in another organism, with citation to Verasztó et al., 2017.

claim: The ciliary plates are a miracidium-specific cell type.
source: The ciliary plates are a miracidium-specific cell type (it is the only life cycle stage that uses motile cilia for locomotion)
evidence: This is established knowledge about the schistosome life cycle.

claim: The ciliary plates are shed within 2–48 hr once inside the snail.
source: and once inside the snail, these plates are shed within 2–48 hr (Meuleman et al., 1978; Poteaux et al., 2023).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Meuleman et al., 1978; Poteaux et al., 2023.

claim: The 16 kDa CaBP (Smp_096390) is clearly important to the function of ciliary plates as it is highly expressed in data collected from both droplet- and plate-based scRNA-seq platforms.
source: The 16 kDa CaBP (Smp_096390) is clearly important to the function of ciliary plates as it is highly expressed in data collected from both droplet- and plate-based scRNA-seq platforms.
evidence: This is an inference based on high expression levels across different scRNA-seq platforms.

claim: Bulk RNA-seq data show that the 16 kDa CaBP gene was previously detected in the late embryonic stage, miracidia, and early mother sporocyst stage.
source: Accordingly, bulk RNA-seq data show this gene was previously detected in the late embryonic stage, miracidia, and early mother sporocyst stage (Lu et al., 2021; Buddenborg et al., 2023).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Lu et al., 2021; Buddenborg et al., 2023.

claim: The transcriptomes of the tegumental cells show a predicted network of genes involved in protein folding, export, and translocation.
source: Between all the ciliary plates sit the ridges of the tegumental cells. The ridges connect to the cell bodies beneath the body wall musculature, and their transcriptomes show a predicted network of genes involved in protein folding, export, and translocation.
evidence: This is based on STRING analysis of tegument marker genes.

claim: Ultrastructural studies have observed abundant RER, ribosomes, Golgi apparatus, and complex carbohydrates in tegumental cell bodies, suggesting they are active in producing exportable proteins.
source: This is consistent with ultrastructural studies that have observed abundant RER, ribosomes, Golgi apparatus, and complex carbohydrates in these cell bodies, suggesting they are active in producing exportable proteins (Meuleman et al., 1978; Pan, 1980).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Meuleman et al., 1978; Pan, 1980.

claim: Large numbers of membrane-bound vesicles were observed in tegumental cells and thought to become part of the new tegument membrane (syncytium) that rapidly forms around the mother sporocyst during the early stages of transformation.
source: Large numbers of membrane-bound vesicles were also observed and thought to become part of the new tegument membrane (syncytium) that rapidly forms around the mother sporocyst during the early stages of transformation, protecting the mother sporocyst from attack by the snails' amoebocytes (Pan, 1980).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Pan, 1980.

claim: The RNA velocity analysis has revealed dynamic genes that may be crucial in the maturation of the tegument cells across the miracidium to sporocyst life cycle transition.
source: The RNA velocity analysis has revealed dynamic genes that may be crucial in the maturation of the tegument cells across this life cycle transition, and in turn, for evasion of host defences and parasite survival.
evidence: This is based on RNA velocity analysis.

claim: Many of the molecular regulators and markers of adult tegument biogenesis are expressed in the miracidia and sporocyst stem and tegument cells, indicating that there is a conserved molecular programme for the development of the syncytial tegument.
source: Many of the molecular regulators and markers of adult tegument biogenesis (Collins et al., 2016; Wendt et al., 2018; Wendt et al., 2022) are expressed in the miracidia and sporocyst stem and tegument cells, indicating that there is a conserved molecular programme for the development of the syncytial tegument in the mother sporocyst and its maintenance in the adult worm.
evidence: This is based on comparison of gene expression across life stages, with citations to Collins et al., 2016; Wendt et al., 2018; Wendt et al., 2022.

claim: The transcriptomes of the two stem populations in the miracidium suggest they are in different activation states.
source: The transcriptomes of the two stem populations in the miracidium suggest they are in different activation states.
evidence: This is based on GO analysis and marker gene expression.

claim: This finding aligns with the discovery of two stem cell populations in the mother sporocyst that have different proliferation kinetics.
source: This finding aligns with the discovery of two stem cell populations in the mother sporocyst that have different proliferation kinetics (Wang et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Wang et al., 2013.

claim: The pre-activated state of Delta/Phi stem cells in the miracidia may signify that they are the first population to proliferate once the miracidium transforms into the mother sporocyst inside the snail.
source: The pre-activated state of Delta/Phi stem cells in the miracidia may signify that they are the first population to proliferate once the miracidium transforms into the mother sporocyst inside the snail.
evidence: This is speculation based on the observed activation state.

claim: The finding that eled and many of the germline-specific regulatory programme components are expressed in some miracidia Kappa cells suggests that when a miracidium hatches, the cells that will contribute to the germline may already be segregated.
source: The finding that eled, and many of the germline-specific regulatory programme components, are expressed in some miracidia Kappa cells suggests that when a miracidium hatches, the cells that will contribute to the germline may already be segregated and the molecular regulatory programme that differentiates somatic (Delta/Phi) and germ cell (Kappa) lineages is present.
evidence: This is an inference based on expression of germline-specific genes.

claim: The presence of spliced-only copies of the germline defining genes eled and boule could suggest that they are maternal transcripts that have been restricted to the primordial germ cells during embryogenesis.
source: Intriguingly, the presence of spliced-only copies of the germline defining genes eled and boule could suggest that they are maternal transcripts that have been restricted to the primordial germ cells during embryogenesis, as is the case in Zebrafish embryos (Fishman et al., 2023).
evidence: This is speculation based on the observation of spliced-only transcripts, with citation to Fishman et al., 2023.

claim: An alternative explanation for the presence of spliced-only copies of eled and boule is that unspliced transcripts exist but their abundance was below the threshold for detection.
source: An alternative explanation is that unspliced transcripts exist for these lowly expressed genes but their abundance was below our threshold for detection.
evidence: This is an alternative explanation for the observation.

claim: The degree of transcriptomic sexual difference was most evident in the Delta/Phi and Kappa stem cell clusters, with no distinct clustering by sex observed in other cell clusters.
source: This degree of transcriptomic sexual difference was most evident in the Delta/Phi and Kappa stem cell clusters, with no distinct clustering by sex observed in other cell clusters.
evidence: This is based on clustering analysis of cells with and without sex chromosome genes.

claim: Incomplete gene dosage compensation in the miracidium could explain the sex-biased clustering of stem cells.
source: This could be explained by incomplete gene dosage compensation in the miracidium.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observed sex-biased clustering.

claim: Tissue-specific variation could add a further dimension to the role of dosage compensation in schistosomes.
source: Following investigations of differences in gene dosage compensation across developmental stages using bulk RNA-seq (Picard et al., 2019), our study suggests tissue-specific variation could add a further dimension to the role of dosage compensation in schistosomes.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observed tissue-specific differences in sex-biased gene expression, with citation to Picard et al., 2019.

claim: A similar phenomenon of tissue-specific dosage compensation has been described in mouse embryonic stem cells and in Drosophila.
source: A similar phenomenon has been described in mouse embryonic stem cells and in Drosophila, where a precise regulation of a gene-by-gene dosage compensation mechanism is critical to the proper development of specific tissues and organs, such as the wing and eye (Valsecchi et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Valsecchi et al., 2018.

claim: Sex differences in undifferentiated stem cells have not been reported in later stages of the schistosome life cycle.
source: In contrast to the miracidium, sex differences in undifferentiated stem cells have not been reported in later stages of the schistosome life cycle (Wang et al., 2018; Diaz Soria et al., 2020; Wendt et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Wang et al., 2018; Diaz Soria et al., 2020; Wendt et al., 2020.

claim: It may not have been possible to detect sex differences in stem cells in earlier studies because scRNA-seq data were mapped onto older versions of the genome, where the sex chromosomes were not as well defined.
source: In fact, it may not have been possible to detect these differences in earlier studies because scRNA-seq data were mapped onto older versions of the genome, where the sex chromosomes were not as well defined (Buddenborg et al., 2021).
evidence: This is speculation about why sex differences were not detected in previous studies, with citation to Buddenborg et al., 2021.

claim: The present study has benefited from a high level of coverage, enabling differences in stem cells to be more easily discerned.
source: In addition to using an improved reference annotation, the present study has also benefited from a high level of coverage, enabling differences in stem cells to be more easily discerned.
evidence: This is a statement about the advantages of the current study.

claim: The current understanding of schistosome development is that differentiated somatic cells of the miracidium do not continue into the daughter sporocyst stage, the cercariae and beyond; it is the stem cells that persist and differentiate into the cell types of the subsequent life stages.
source: The current understanding of schistosome development is that differentiated somatic cells of the miracidium do not continue into the daughter sporocyst stage, the cercariae and beyond; it is the stem cells that persist and differentiate into the cell types of the subsequent life stages (Wang et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Wang et al., 2018.

claim: All miracidium somatic cells are miracidium-only cells.
source: In this respect, all miracidium somatic cells are miracidium-only cells.
evidence: This is an inference based on the understanding that somatic cells do not persist beyond the miracidium stage.

claim: The transcriptional signatures of miracidium somatic cells are similar to comparable tissue types at later stages.
source: Our atlas shows that their transcriptional signatures are similar to comparable tissue types at later stages (Diaz Soria et al., 2020; Wendt et al., 2020; Diaz Soria et al., 2024)
evidence: This is based on comparison of gene expression across life stages, with citations to Diaz Soria et al., 2020; Wendt et al., 2020; Diaz Soria et al., 2024.

claim: There may be conserved tissue-specific molecular developmental programmes that are deployed multiple times during the complex life cycle.
source: and that there may be conserved tissue-specific molecular developmental programmes that are deployed multiple times during the complex life cycle.
evidence: This is an inference based on the similarity of transcriptional signatures across life stages.
